samples.summary: Two other "exit the list" paths still hardcode 'paragraph', so they destroy the newly-retained headingLevel
samples.evidence: `Doc.deleteBackward` (document.ts:263-265) does `if (curBlock.type === 'list-item' && getBlockTextLength(curBlock) === 0) this.setBlockType(pos.blockId, 'paragraph')` and `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:298-300) does the same for Enter on an empty list item. Both are user-visible "remove the bullet" gestures, and both bypass the new `unlistedBlockType` helper — so `setBlockType(..., 'paragraph')` runs `delete block.headingLevel` (memory.ts:251, yorkie-doc-store.ts:1453) and the remembered level is gone forever. The new doc comment on `Block.headingLevel` claims "removing the list restores it (see `unlistedBlockType`)", but only the three `toggleList` sites honour that: emptying a bulleted Heading 2 and pressing Backspace (or Enter) yields body text and the level cannot be recovered, while the toolbar toggle on the same block yields the heading. The helper was introduced specifically to stop the implementations drifting, and these two call sites already drift.

samples.summary: Splitting a bulleted heading drops headingLevel from the tail block, so the two halves un-list to different block types
samples.evidence: `applySplitBlock` does `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel;` (block-helpers.ts:256-258) and the Yorkie mirror does `if (newBlockType === 'heading' && block.headingLevel !== undefined) afterAttrs.headingLevel = ...` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2049, 2139). Since `Doc.splitBlock` picks `newType = 'list-item'` when splitting a list item (document.ts:324-325), pressing Enter in the middle of a bulleted Heading 2 leaves the first half a list-item carrying headingLevel 2 and the second half a list-item with none. Toggling the bullet off over both blocks in one selection then produces a heading followed by a paragraph from what looked like two identical bullets. The task doc lists split as a non-goal, but with the retention change it is now an observable asymmetry rather than a uniform behaviour.

samples.summary: Yorkie keep-path never writes headingLevel into the CRDT attrs, relying on the assumption that the tree node already carries it
samples.evidence: When `keepHeadingLevel` is true the code only suppresses the `toRemove.push('headingLevel')` (line 1413); `attrs` (line 1383-1390) still contains no `headingLevel`, per the comment "The attribute is already on the node". The cache is then repopulated from `prevHeadingLevel` (line 1458), which is read from the in-memory block, not from the tree. Any state where the cached block has a headingLevel the tree node lacks (e.g. a cache repopulated from a partially-applied remote patch, or a future cache-only mutation such as the direct `headBlock.headingLevel = ...` paste writes in text-editor.ts:3578 before `updateBlockDirect` lands) makes the local editor show a restorable heading while every other peer sees a plain list item, and the divergence is silent. Writing `attrs.headingLevel = String(block.headingLevel)` in the keep branch would make the tree and the cache agree unconditionally.

samples.summary: unlistedBlockType only remembers headings; bulleting a Title/Subtitle still flattens it to a paragraph
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` keys purely off `block.headingLevel`, and `setBlockType` only stashes `headingLevel` for `list-item` (memory.ts:257-262). `title` and `subtitle` blocks carry no `headingLevel`, so bulleting a Title and un-bulleting it still returns `{ type: 'paragraph' }` — exactly the data-loss the change sets out to fix, just for the other two named-style block types (`blockStyleId` treats title/subtitle as first-class styles, named-styles.ts:101-104). The fix is therefore partial and the round-trip invariant documented on `Block.headingLevel` does not hold for all styled blocks.
searchedFor: grep headingLevel across packages/docs/src and packages/frontend/src
grep for any title/subtitle retention in setBlockType implementations

samples.summary: unlistedBlockType propagates an unvalidated headingLevel (out-of-range or NaN) back into a heading block
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` returns `{ headingLevel: block.headingLevel }` with no clamping, and the level on a list item can legitimately be out of the 1-6 `HeadingLevel` range: `docx-importer.ts:242` casts a raw `parseInt` of `Heading N` (N can be 7-9) and `yorkie-doc-store.ts:438` / `docs-tree.ts:409` do `Number(attrs.headingLevel)`, which yields `NaN` for a corrupt attribute — and `NaN !== undefined`, so the guard on line 340 passes. Un-listing such a block writes `headingLevel: NaN`/7 back through `setBlockType`, which serializes it into the CRDT as `"NaN"` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1385). Downstream readers degrade rather than crash (`blockStyleId` clamps, `resolveStyleInline` uses `?.`), so impact is limited to a persistently corrupt attribute, but the helper is the place that turns a previously inert value into a written one.
